summary_zh.motivation: 研究工艺参数对SLM制备NiTi合金相变和拉伸性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过改变激光功率、扫描速度等参数进行SLM成形，并进行表征。
summary_zh.result: 发现工艺参数显著影响相变温度和拉伸强度。
summary_zh.validation: 采用拉伸测试和DSC进行实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of selective laser melting process parameters on the phase transformation behavior and tensile properties of NiTi shape memory alloys.
summary_en.method: NiTi samples were fabricated by SLM with varying laser power and scanning speed, followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Process parameters were found to significantly affect transformation temperatures and tensile strength, enabling tailored properties.
summary_en.validation: The results were validated through tensile testing and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC).

llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical comparison of surgical approaches with no biomechanical FEA, no stress/micromotion quantification, no implant design analysis, and no intact vs implanted femur comparison.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较Supercapsular Percutaneously Assisted入路与传统外侧入路在全髋关节置换术中的早期效果。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性队列研究，纳入两组患者并比较术后临床指标。
summary_zh.result: 微创入路在早期康复方面可能具有优势，但差异有限。
summary_zh.validation: 通过术后随访和临床评分进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare early clinical outcomes between Supercapsular Percutaneously Assisted and lateral approaches in total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A prospective comparative study was conducted with patient cohorts undergoing each surgical approach.
summary_en.result: The minimally invasive approach showed modest benefits in early recovery but no major differences in complications.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through postoperative clinical assessments and follow-up scores.

papers.title: TGase‐Enhanced Microtissue Assembly in 3D‐Printed‐Template‐Scaffold (3D‐MAPS) for Large Tissue Defect Reparation
papers.abstract: Abstract Engineering large and functional tissue constructs with complex structures (e.g., external ear or nose) for reparation and reconstruction of tissue defects remains one of the major challenges in regenerative medicine, which demands abundant cell sources, advanced biofabrication schemes, and satisfactory integration with the host for long‐term efficacy post implantation. Here the ‘Microtissue Assembly in 3D‐Printed‐template‐Scaffold’ (3D‐MAPS), as a platform technology to rapidly fabricate centimeter‐sized functional tissue constructs with complex structures, is developed. 3D‐MAPS facilitates bottom‐up assembly of large‐scale manufactured microtissues within the 3D‐printed hollow polymeric templates with pre‐defined architectures. The assembly and fusion of 2×10 6 mesenchymal stem cell–based microtissues within the defined 3D‐printed template is further enhanced by addition of a natural protein crosslinker (i.e., transglutaminase (TGase)), and thereby achieves construction of centimeter‐sized tissue with high cell viability and mechanical stability in vitro within 30 min. Further in vivo implantation of the 3D‐MAPS‐fabricated ear‐like tissue construct in rabbit models assisted by flap prefabrication technique results in increased structural vascular support and strengthened functional survival. Thus, the TGase‐enhanced 3D‐MAPS demonstrates its potential and feasibility as a powerful biofabrication platform for tissue engineering application.

summary_en.motivation: To engineer large, functional tissue constructs with complex structures for repairing tissue defects.
summary_en.method: A platform (3D-MAPS) that assembles microtissues within 3D-printed hollow templates, enhanced by transglutaminase crosslinking.
summary_en.result: Centimeter-sized ear-like tissue constructs with high cell viability and mechanical stability were fabricated within 30 minutes and showed increased vascular support in rabbit models.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell viability and mechanical tests, followed by in vivo implantation in a rabbit model.
